newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares sharp slide stabilises at close.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares sharp slide stabilises at close.

text.p: Singapore shares slid sharply in late afternoon trade on Tuesday after the United States said it had attacked Iraqi air defences, but the falls stabilised shortly before the market closed, dealers said.
"Buying withdrew and the fall was further exaggerated by the thin volume," said a sales director with a foreign brokerage.
"The bigwigs (blue chips) were being dumped. But there was a fair bit of recovery by a spread or so in the last hour of trading," said a dealer with a local brokerage.
The Straits Times Industrials Index fell 23.54 points to 2,105.26, back up from an earlier drop of more than 30 points.
Market volume was a modest 92.62 million shares with declines thumping advances by 260 to 78.
Singapore Press foreign topped the losers, dropping S$0.60 to S$23.30. SIA foreign also fell S$0.50 to S$14.30.
Malaysian Resources was up on news of a 200 million ringgit joint venture agreement with Singapore's Pidemco Land to build two condominiums in Kuala Lumpur. It rose S$0.12 to S$4.42.
Bucking the trend of an electronics sell-down, PCI was most traded with 4.53 million shares changing hands. It closed S$0.06 higher at S$0.855.
back further on Tuesday morning, continuing a slow seven-day slide which has clipped around 70 points off the benchmark Straits Times Industrials Index (STII).

"I really don't know why it is so weak," said one institutional dealer. "There's a general disinterest in the market overseas...It may be adjustments because of the changes in the Morgan Stanley Asian indices." Morgan Stanley's recently down-weighted Singapore in its Asian stock indices.
By the 0430 GMT lunchtime close, the STII stood at 2,117.71 points, down 11.09. Volume was 32.7 million.

Top of the actives list at midday was printed circuit-board maker PCI Ltd, which saw its shares rise to a high of Singapore $0.93, up 17 percent, after a cross of just over two million shares in the company at S$0.80 cents each.
Another active share was trading firm Causeway Investment, which saw a cross of one million shares at S$1.45 each. Last month, the firm denied takeover rumours after a rash of similar crosses.
